rationale: A is clearly better because its 40 tasks × 5 languages allocation actually fits the 200-run budget, uses matched tasks to control task difficulty, and gives an actionable plan for reporting uncertainty. Its power calculations contain notable errors—the stated noncentral chi-square powers cannot fall below the 5% test size, and the resulting MDE claims are inconsistent—so they should not be trusted verbatim. However, B is fatally infeasible: 5 × 3 × 10 × 13 equals 1,950 runs, not 195, invalidating its allocation and all downstream power claims; its variance calculation also incorrectly retains task variance in a matched within-task language contrast.
